title: The Real Reason You Procrastinate Important Tasks
hook: Why do we delay important tasks, even when we know better?

narration.text: Your brain values immediate rewards much more than future ones.
This is called temporal discounting, and it explains a lot.
A treat now feels more valuable than a bigger treat later.
So, finishing a big project feels less urgent than watching TV.
The further away the reward, the less compelling it seems.
This bias makes it hard to start tasks with distant payoffs.
It is a fundamental part of human decision-making.
Understanding this can help you trick your brain into starting.
What important task are you putting off right now?

description: Ever wondered why you keep putting off important tasks, even when you know they are critical? It is not just laziness, it is a psychological phenomenon called temporal discounting. Discover how your brain prioritises immediate gratification over future rewards, impacting your productivity.
topic: Why you procrastinate on important tasks, explaining temporal discounting.
